description.narrative:
The Oxfam / ATAD response will provide complementary activities to meet urgent needs. 5,950 IDPs and very poor guests in Barsalogho (850 HH - 1,733 girls, 1,362 women, 1,285 boys and 1,570 men) will benefit from: a distribution of 40,000 CFA francs/month over 3 months (7 persons/household, according to the CWG), distribution of white energy water for 1,100 CFA francs over 3 months; awareness<(>&<)> screening, distribution of fortified nutritional flour to 1264 children aged 6-23 months (2.5kg/child/month) recommended bythe Food Sec Cluster and the Nutrition Directorate, covering energy needs and acute malnutrition.
Against diseases and Covid-19, 7,500 people (IDPs and hosts) in Barsalogho will benefit from access to safe drinking water and WASH infrastructure (Sphere): 2 boreholes with human powered pumps (HPP), transformation of an HPP well into an autonomous water point (AWP) and rehabilitation of an AWP; construction/rehabilitation of excreta/solid waste management infrastructure; improvement of knowledge and practice (hygiene and Covid-19) (awareness-raising and distribution of hygiene kits).
Concerning protection, the action will enhance the safety, dignity and improve the protection situation of 6,500 IDPs and hosts (60% women <(>&<)> girls – 2800 in Kaya <(>&<)> 3700 in Barsalogho) through: monitoring and referral of protection cases to specialised services; capacity building and community-based protection mechanisms (4CPC); community sensitisation and advocacy, facilitation of access to care services <(>&<)> support in 300 protection kits (flashlight, radio, mats, child and elderly ointment for cold management, and blanket for elderly) and installation of 40 solar street lights. Key aspects of protection will be integrated into the WASH and EFSL components to ensure the safety and dignity of beneficiaries by facilitating meaningful and equitable access to activities, which will be subject to change according to the needs of the communities consulted.
Complementarity will be sought with other NGOs (MSF, DRC, IRC, etc.) with whom Oxfam collaborates within clusters (Co-facilitator of the food/sec cluster, strategic orientation committee of the Wash cluster, protection cluster, lead sub-clusterfor accountability and community engagement). The cases of GBV identified by the CPCs (Oxfam) will be referred to the care services(Alima mobile clinics, IRC psychosocial services). Due to Covid19, door-to-door and small group exchanges will be encouraged while respecting barrier measures.
ATAD will work with Oxfam inBarsalogho, with CARE in Rollo; so it could assign different teams to the areas and work in a complementary way

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Intermon is a member of Oxfam International, a confederation of 17 independent national organisations working in more than 90countries. Oxfam works on six goals that support the shared vision of a just world without poverty: help people claim their right to a better life; champion equal rights for women; saving lives, now and in the future; safeguard global food supplies; help people claim a fairer share of natural resources; and increase money for basic services. For 70 years, Oxfam has been running emergency responses, development projects and campaigning at the grass roots level to tackle poverty.

comment.narrative: In total, 7346 people, including 3526 women, 2498 men, 882 young girls, 440 young boys and 54 people living with a disability have information on their rights and the relevant services available in their areas. This represents an achievement rate of 113%compared to the initial target of 6500 people. This was possible thanks to the efforts of the members of the Community Protection Committees (CPC) in referring cases of protection such as rape and physical aggression to the care services; the holding of community and small group sensitization sessions on various protection themes such as social cohesion, women's participation, early marriage, human rights, integration of marginalized groups and equality; The dissemination of two maps of available services in the target areas for self-referral purposes; the continuous and punctual dissemination of messages on social cohesion, the right to education, the rights of displaced people and the referral circuit produced by the GBV sub-cluster in the North Center.

comment.narrative: The members of the Community Protection Committees (CPCs), local authorities and community leaders in the communes of Kaya and Barsalgho received capacity building on the themes of protection, gender-based violence, GBV case referral and social cohesion in order to better equip them to identify protection risks and threats in their context and to find actions to prevent, mitigate or solve them. At the end of the training sessions, each CPC received support in terms of Information, Education and Communication (IEC) materials, including picture boxes, posters, reporting registers and operating expenses, which helped them carry out sensitization, referral and advocacy activities at the local level based on the protection and gender issues identified in their community protection plans. A total of 71 people, including 26 men, 17 women, 14 girls and 14 boys, were reached by these capacity building sessions. This represents a 79% completion rate compared to the initial target of 90 people. This implementation rate is justified by the limited travel of the project teams to the commune of Barsalgho because of the GANEs. Some activities, such as the training of local authorities and community leaders, were redefined so as not to put participants at risk. Planned to be held in both communes (Barsalgho and Kaya), the activity was carried out exclusively in Kaya. The remaining funds were used to balance other lines such as support for the operating costs of community protection committees and the production of sensitization materials on protection, rights and gender-based violence.

comment.narrative: 2,800 people, including 1,163 women, 957 men, 386 girls and 294 boys, were affected by the implementation of specific GBV prevention measures, which represents a 100% completion rate. This was possible thanks to community awareness-raising activities on GBV, the distribution of protection kits and the installation of solar street lamps in IDP sites. Out of the total number of people reached, 300 people (254 women and 46 men) each received a protection kit composed of a radio and a flashlight. The lamps allowed the beneficiaries to light their shelters or to move easily at night to go to places like toilets and reduce the risks of aggression or possible gender-based violence (physical and sexual aggression). As for the radios, they allowed women and men to follow the awareness and safety information in order to adopt behaviors adapted to the situation and the environment. In collaboration with members of the CPCs and local authorities, monthly consultations were undertaken with the communities for concerted decisions on the composition of the protection kits to be distributed and the choice of the most appropriate locations for the installation of thirty-forty lamp posts in the commune of Kaya. The objective of this activity was to facilitate access to information, restore dignity and prevent the integrity of women and girls from the risks of GBV when accessing toilets and other basic services in the sites in the evening and at night due to the darkness and to improve security conditions in the IDP sitesand on certain roads leading to public services such as health centers and sanitation services. This practical humanitarian assistance provided material support to women and girls to prevent the risk of GBV and improve the safety of the most vulnerable people from existing threats

comment.narrative: The implementation of the project in the communes of Barsalogho and Kaya has enabled 11,376 people (7,660 women and 3,716 men) to benefit from a package of multi-sectoral holistic approaches (10,024 people with food security, 11,376 with WASH and 7346 with protection activities.), this led to an achievement rate of 110% compared to the planned target. The food and nutritional needs of vulnerable IDP and host households were covered through food assistance via the cash transfer modality in the amount of 60,000 XOF or Euro 91 /household/month for two months for the benefit of 1,075 households (10,024 persons) made up of 804 IDP households (75% of beneficiaries) and 271 host community (25% of beneficiaries). The distribution of beneficiaries by gender shows 64% of households headed by women and 36% of households headed by men. In addition, in order to prevent malnutrition among people at risk (children aged between 6 and 23 months) and Pregnant and Lactating Women (PLW), 585 children aged between 6 and 23months from targeted IDP and host households benefited from distributions of enriched flour (2.5 kg/child/month) and screening for malnutrition for 3 months simultaneously with the cash food assistance. Also, 603 PLW from beneficiary households received nutritional supplements of 2,1 Kg/ PLW/ month for 3 months. Finally, sensitization of PLW was conducted simultaneously with the distribution of fortified flour on the techniques of preparing fortified porridges, food rationing, the consequences of malnutrition, the importance of prenatal visits, and the advantages of infant breastfeeding. Thanks to the transformation/rehabilitation of water points, the realization of sanitation works and the hygiene promotion activities carried out at 100%, 11,376 persons (2,174 men; 5,020 women; 2,640 girls and 1,542 boys) have reinforced their access to safe drinking water, hygiene and sanitation services.
